title: Chapter 8 Quiz: Production‑Ready Features (Actuator)
description: Test your knowledge of Spring Boot Actuator endpoints, configuration, and customization.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Spring Boot Actuator?
options: To provide production‑ready monitoring and management endpoints
questions.explanation: Actuator adds endpoints for health checks, metrics, environment info, and more – essential for monitoring apps in production.

questions.question: By default, all Actuator endpoints are exposed over HTTP.
questions.explanation: Only /health and /info are exposed by default. Others must be explicitly enabled.

questions.question: The base path for Actuator endpoints is _________ by default.
questions.explanation: Actuator endpoints are mounted under /actuator, e.g., /actuator/health.

questions.question: Which endpoint would you use to see the list of all Spring beans?
questions.explanation: /beans lists all beans in the application context.

questions.question: The /health endpoint can be customized with custom health indicators.
questions.explanation: You can implement HealthIndicator to add custom checks to the /health endpoint.

questions.question: Which property enables detailed health information?
questions.explanation: management.endpoint.health.show-details=always reveals component health details.

questions.question: To see the current memory usage, you would query _________.
questions.explanation: Metrics are available under /metrics with metric names like jvm.memory.used.

questions.question: How can you add custom information to the /info endpoint?
questions.explanation: You can add custom info via properties (info.app.name=...) or programmatically with InfoContributor.

questions.question: The /env endpoint is safe to expose in production without any restrictions.
questions.explanation: /env can reveal sensitive configuration values like passwords or API keys; it should be secured or disabled in production.

questions.question: Which property enables all Actuator endpoints?
questions.explanation: Use management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* to expose all endpoints over HTTP.

questions.question: To change the base path of Actuator endpoints, set _________.
questions.explanation: This property changes the prefix for Actuator endpoints.

questions.question: What does the /loggers endpoint allow you to do?
options: View and change log levels at runtime
questions.explanation: /loggers lets you retrieve and modify log levels for packages/classes without restarting.

questions.question: Actuator endpoints can be accessed over JMX as well as HTTP.
questions.explanation: By default, Actuator endpoints are exposed over JMX and optionally over HTTP.

questions.question: Which annotation can you use to create a custom health indicator?
questions.explanation: You create a bean that implements HealthIndicator and annotate it with @Component (or @Service).

questions.question: The _________ endpoint shows all URL mappings (controllers).
questions.explanation: /mappings lists all @RequestMapping routes.

questions.question: How can you exclude the /env endpoint from being exposed?
questions.explanation: You can exclude it via management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude, or disable it entirely with management.endpoint.env.enabled=false.

questions.question: You can use Actuator to change log levels at runtime without redeploying.
questions.explanation: The /loggers endpoint allows POST requests to update log levels.

questions.question: What does the /metrics endpoint provide?
questions.explanation: /metrics provides a wide range of metrics including JVM, system, HTTP, and custom metrics.

questions.question: The default HTTP port for Actuator is the same as the application port (usually _________ ).
questions.explanation: Actuator endpoints are served on the same port as the main application by default.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a built‑in Actuator endpoint?
questions.explanation: /admin is not a standard Actuator endpoint. /trace is (for request tracing).
